I continue to believe that China will do to the memory markets what Japan did to the US companies in the early 1980s and the Koreans did to the Japanese companies in the early 2000s. But even if that is the case, history would suggest at least a near-term rally is coming in the semiconductor sector. This would seem to be true even if we have seen THE TOP in the overall AI trade much like during the bursting of the internet bubble in 2000-2002.

To be clear, I do not think we have seen THE TOP in the overall AI trade. I believe the advent of Agentic AI in January with formalization of OpenClaw and the follow on innovations should give the overall AI trade room to run into 2027. Call it Agentic AI for the non-techies. That started in September with Muse from $META followed by Dots from OpenAI and the Co-Pilot revamp by $MSFT in October for enterprise. I expect most LLM vendors to have their own easy to use Agent out before too long.

The bottom line is even if we have seen THE TOP, the odds based on history are high for at least a short-term rally.

As we said at the time, "money has to reside somewhere, and Privy builds the world's best programmable vaults."

Since then, the Privy team has executed exceptionally well: assets in Privy wallets have grown ~25x, monthly active developers are up ~3x, revenue is up ~9x, and Privy now facilitates nearly $25B of monthly transaction volume. @tryramp, @Deel, @Klarna, @felixpago, @HyperliquidX, and thousands of other businesses are building embedded banking functionality on Privy.

At Stripe, we're deeply integrating Privy into Treasury, @Link, and Connect. In each case, it's accelerating our global expansion, and enabling us to build better functionality faster. (Coming soon: @Link balances.)

We're also seeing that Privy's wallet infrastructure is the ideal substrate for agents to transact and earn -- live today with @merit_systems, @orthogonal_sh, @Nevermined_ai, @prlnet, and more. Developers prefer programmable financial infrastructure, but agents need it. We expect that the agentic economy will continue to grow extremely quickly.

The Privy team has maintained remarkable product velocity, with major launches this year including deposit addresses, earning on Privy balances, digital asset accounts, custodial wallets, and Stripe's own stablecoin cards.

It's also been neat to see how Privy has been accelerated by Stripe, with better onramps, @stablecoin payment rails and licenses, Stripe's fiat capabilities and issuing stack, and integration with @Tempo.

Together, we're building one API for holding stablecoin balances and earning yield, moving money in and out of fiat, and orchestrating spend with cards. We still have a lot of work to do, not least in integrating everything across Privy, Bridge, and the rest of Stripe -- there's been so much feature and functionality expansion that we haven't yet had much time to reconcile everything. YES BANK AT1 VERDICT: ₹8,415 CRORE CASH OUTFLOW? NOT SO FAST!
Several media reports and X handles appear to be confusing the reinstatement of AT1 bonds with an immediate ₹8,415 crore cash repayment obligation. These are fundamentally different concepts

1. AT1 bonds are PERPETUAL, not conventional debt.
They have no contractual maturity or mandatory principal repayment date. Reinstatement of ₹8,415 crore of AT1 instruments does NOT automatically translate into an equivalent cash outflow

2. AT1 coupons are discretionary and NON-CUMULATIVE
Unlike conventional bonds, banks can cancel AT1 coupons subject to regulatory and contractual conditions. Cancelled coupons do not accumulate as arrears

3. Understand Dividend PUSHER vs STOPPER clauses
• Pusher: In conventional perpetual securities, payment of dividends on ordinary shares may trigger an obligation to pay coupons on the perpetual instruments.
• Stopper: If AT1 coupons are cancelled, the bank may be restricted from paying dividends to ordinary shareholders or undertaking discretionary share buybacks

Crucially, under RBI's Basel III AT1 framework, these mechanisms cannot override the bank's discretion to cancel AT1 coupons. YES Bank's actual bond terms govern

4. CET1 impact ≠ immediate liquidity impact.
Reversing the 2020 AT1 write-off could reduce reported CET1 capital, with corresponding recognition of AT1 capital subject to regulatory eligibility. This is a significant capital adequacy issue, but not necessarily a cash drain

5. SMBC’s investment- A strategic investment
SMBC acquired its strategic stake in YES Bank while the AT1 litigation was publicly known. A sophisticated global banking investor would ordinarily assess such a material legal and regulatory risk during due diligence, although its actual conclusions are not public

The Supreme Court judgment is important, but reporting ₹8,415 crore as an immediate cash liability risks misleading investors

The real questions are CET1 treatment, coupon obligations under the Information Memorandum, RBI's regulatory position and implementation of the judgment

AT1 reinstatement ≠ AT1 redemption. Accounting capital ≠ cash flow.

Want to know the ultimate test of a trader?

Hint: It isn’t how much you make when the market is easy. It’s what you do after a devastating loss that completely defines your career. [02:39]

This month, one of our top trading desks at SMB Capital took a tough loss. They were long a position when an unexpected, intervening event dropped out of nowhere and hammered the stock.

The damage? Down over $3 million. [00:13]

In prop trading, that plunges a desk straight into what we call "the hole" [00:13]. Before these guys see another dollar of payout, they have to grind back every single dollar of those millions just to get back to flat [00:23].

Bad beats happen. Losses happen. It flat-out sucks, you feel it right in the pit of your stomach, and the pain lingers [02:32].

It is what you do after the loss that matters—not the loss. [09:10] The $3M deficit matters very little in the long run compared to how the team and its individual contributors respond right now [02:49].

In our latest video, I broke down the exact 6-step blueprint this elite desk is using to climb out of their hole [03:26]:

1. Run a Forensic AAR (After Action Report): Stripping emotion from P&L [03:42]. The team leader didn't bury the loss in a large pepperoni pizza and a bottle of red wine [04:47]. He delivered a candid, constructive autopsy: owning his mistakes, analyzing hedge execution, and praising the quick-thinking put purchases that saved another $2M in damage [04:20].

2. Collaborate Across the Desk: As Ray Dalio observed, viewing the market through one pair of eyes means missing critical information [05:04]. On our desk, an impressive junior 7-figure producer respectfully pushed back on the star's self-critique, arguing the entry add was technically sound and purely hit by an exogenous intervening shock [05:32]. That open debate is where real edge compounds [06:01].

3. Bring the Trade to the Firm Crucible: The desk brought the trade to partners, risk managers, and mentors like @theonelanceb [06:13]. Risk reviewed limits, senior partners coordinated tech solutions for faster news execution, and coaches challenged the floor [06:23]. A painful rip becomes rocket fuel when your entire firm has your back [06:50].

4. Chip Away with One Good Trade: As Market Wizard Marty Schwartz famously said, greatness isn't hitting home runs; it's stringing together singles and doubles [07:02]. No desperate YOLO swings. The team leader set the tone: "I am just going to chip away at these losses." One Good Trade. And then One Good Trade. And then One Good Trade [07:25].

5. Grounded Veteran Optimism: As Colin Powell noted, "Perpetual optimism is a force multiplier." [07:49] The senior leader reminded the desk that drawdowns are temporary, he's clawed out of every hole before, and each slump made him a better trader [08:09]. Veteran leadership eliminates panic [08:26].

6. Game Plan High-Conviction Catalysts: Don't predict—anticipate [08:37]. The team mapped out high-opportunity environments ahead (like the Anthropic IPO and potential Q4 momentum) to deploy asymmetric risk when the setup aligns [08:48].

The market will knock you down, but your career isn't defined by the brutal blow—it is defined by the grit, discipline, and character you display when you stand back up.

It is what you do after the loss that matters.
